_comment: Hard rules applied after everything else, for flights that cannot legally operate today. Wikipedia pages can lag; these make sure a stale listing never puts a banned route on the map.

closed_countries.UA: Ukrainian airspace has been closed to civil flights since February 2022.

closed_airports._comment: Airports with no flights though some Wikipedia pages still list routes to them; routes touching them are dropped. Russia's southern airports closed in February 2022 and not reopened as of October 2026 (Krasnodar reopened in 2025, Elista and Gelendzhik in 2024): Ural Airlines' list of closed airports and russiable.com. Port-au-Prince: Sunrise Airways' notices, juno7.ht, FAA NOTAM A0046/26. Sana'a: safeairspace.net/yemen. Goma and Bukavu: ktpress.rw, africaunscrambled.substack.com, Australia's Smartraveller. Thandwe and Bhamo: borderlens.com, Wikipedia. Axum, Shire and Humera: the US Embassy in Addis Ababa's alert of 15 October 2026, avionio.com.

limited_airports._comment: Airports reopened only in part after a closure, whose Wikipedia tables and passenger totals still describe them before it: only the routes and airlines reported flying are kept, the old total isn't used to scale estimates, and the airport's page says why.

KRT.note: Closed by the war in April 2023. Domestic flights resumed in February 2026, and a few international ones from April (Sudanair to Cairo, Badr Airlines to Istanbul); Port Sudan is still Sudan's main gateway.

suspended._comment: Airlines that stopped flying somewhere though Wikipedia's tables still list them, as of October 2026: build_routes.py's drop_suspended() takes them off those routes. 'airlines' is a list of names, 'foreign' (all but the country's own, less 'except') or 'home:XX' (all of a country's); 'at' airports or 'countries' say where, and 'with' limits a rule to routes that also touch those countries.

blocked_country_pairs.why: The US, Canada, the UK, the EU, Norway, Iceland and Switzerland closed their airspace to Russian (and Belarusian) airlines in 2021–22, and their own airlines stopped flying there.
Turkish airlines stopped flying to Israel in late 2023, and Israeli airlines don't fly to Turkey.

blocked_routes.why: Air France suspended Ouagadougou in August 2023 and hasn't returned; Ouagadougou's page still lists it.
Air France suspended Niamey in August 2023, when Niger closed its airspace to French airlines; Niamey's page still lists it.

moved_airports.why: Luanda's international flights moved to the new Dr. António Agostinho Neto airport; other airports' pages still name the old one, which keeps domestic and private flights.
Techo International replaced Phnom Penh International in September 2025.
Hamad International replaced the old Doha International for airline flights in 2014.

cities._comment: Airports are grouped into cities by the first place their Wikipedia infobox says they serve (all of London's six link to London), keeping those within 85 km of the group's busiest airport, in the same country, with 100,000 passengers or more. 'add' makes groups Wikipedia's links miss (Tokyo's airports link to 'Tokyo' and 'Greater Tokyo Area') and takes their airports out of any other group; 'rename' fixes names the cleanup doesn't ('Keihanshin' is Osaka).

airspace._comment: Airspace airlines go around, as of October 2026. Each rule names the countries (Natural Earth codes) or regions to avoid and whose airlines avoid them: 'all', or country codes and groups, an airline's country being the one most of its routes touch. A route never avoids a country it flies to or from. Partial closures (parts of Saudi Arabia's Jeddah FIR, the waters of the Persian Gulf) aren't modelled. Review these when the monthly rebuild runs and update 'as_of'.

rules.name: Iran
rules.source: Open on paper since mid-2026 (the east only), but avoided by almost every foreign airline since the strikes of February 2026; EASA CZIB-2026-04, the FAA's prohibition

rules.name: Conflict zones
rules.source: EASA conflict zone bulletins that advise against all altitudes: Iraq (CZIB-2026-05), Lebanon (-06), Sudan (CZIB-2023-01), Yemen over land (CZIB-2017-07); France's and Italy's notices for Iraq. Afghanistan, Syria, Libya, Mali and Somalia aren't avoided: their warnings now cover only flights below FL260-FL320, and airliners cross them above it

rules.name: North Korea
rules.source: Avoided by foreign airlines since its missile tests over the Sea of Japan

rules.name: The Tibetan Plateau
rules.source: The Tibetan Plateau, Karakoram and Pamirs: if a cabin lost pressure there, there'd be no lower ground to descend to, so airliners keep to the few routes over it they're equipped for
